text:
Tampa Bay won this one by getting two goals in 36 seconds early and then holding on, and the play mostly backed that up. Anthony Cirelli tipped one in at 5:26 of the first, John Carlson scored from the point at 6:02, and the Lightning had the first period almost to themselves, outchancing Minnesota 1.34 to 0.61 in expected goals. Both of those early shots were low-percentage looks (8 and 3 percent), so the 2-0 lead was a little generous to the way the chances were drawn up.

Minnesota took over the middle of the game. Quinn Hughes, who logged 32:36 and drove a team-best 2.59 expected goals for, scored at 2:32 of the second to cut it to 1-2. Carlson answered on a power-play slap shot at 4:55 for his second of the night, and the Wild never got closer than one. Blake Coleman scored on the power play at 14:01 after leading all skaters with 6 shots on goal, but the third period was even (1.07 to 1.05 in expected goals) and Minnesota could not find the equalizer.

Over 60 minutes, Tampa Bay generated 3.49 expected goals to Minnesota's 3.06 and won 57 percent of simulated replays, so the win was earned, though not by much. Carlson fired 9 shots and was named first star, and Dennis Hildeby stopped 34 of 36, a hair better than the chances against him suggested. Jesper Wallstedt was fine at the other end, but the early deficit was too much.
